title: Repair and damage, not just average steering gain
dataset: Historical CEFR v2 development episodes; p6 vs raw, same scenario/level/seed; different arm histories
outcomeDefinition: Grammar AND naturalness >=3 on the original 0-4 rubric. This is NOT the full 9/10 promotion requirement.

effects.scale: historical 0-4 ordinal judgment, not a new 0-10 score

metadata.interpretation: Equal-weight family effects; bootstrap intervals assume independent, representative families. Sign-flip p-values assume independent family effects symmetric about zero under the null. Exact enumeration is a symmetry test, not automatically a valid randomization test. Few families imply discrete p-values and unstable intervals; rows within a family are not independent replicates.

Reversed positions are mapped to original candidate identities. Descriptive consistency only, not a preference ranking or independent evidence.

recognitionOrderControl.interpretation: This is the target model's A/B recognition, not a judge calibration: B-only selections flip candidate identity under reversed order.

metadata.interpretation: Descriptive paired judge agreement, not independent evidence of correctness or validity. Correlated judges can agree while sharing errors; abstention counts include all incomplete pairs.

reservedJudgeAgreement.interpretation: Two prompts of the same model family rating ordinal CEFR level; descriptive agreement is not independent validity or human calibration.

limitations: Retrospective analysis of already-examined data; not a new confirmatory test.
Bootstrap resamples families, not tokens or repeated seeds. Six families yield coarse/low-power inference.
Sign-flip inference assumes symmetry/exchangeability of family effects; no randomized arm assignment is claimed.
Holm adjustment covers only the four displayed endpoints, not all prior search choices.
CEFR levels are ordinal; no continuous proficiency or 9/10 success is inferred from level separation.
New component random-controls will be recorded separately and not pooled with the historical single-direction controls.
